lead: A modern car carries from about twenty to over a hundred electric motors: the starter, wipers, window lifts, seat adjusters, blower and radiator fans, fuel and water pumps, and in hybrid and electric cars the traction motor. Most are direct-current (DC) machines; the alternator and the traction motors are three-phase machines. Each motor is sized for how it is used: a starter runs for seconds, a radiator fan for hours. That pattern of use is its duty type, and the rating on its nameplate is only valid for that duty.
prereq: You need: the force on a current in a magnetic field and Faraday's law from physics, the alternator and starter motor from the starting and charging topic, and solenoids, relays and stepper motors for the H-bridge.

blocks.text: A DC motor has a stationary field (permanent magnets or a field winding) and a rotating armature whose coils are fed through brushes and a commutator. The commutator reverses each coil's current as it passes the poles, so the torque always acts the same way. As the armature turns it also works as a generator and makes a back emf E that opposes the supply.
E = kΦ ω, V = E + I Ra, T = kΦ I

E is back emf in V; kΦ is the machine constant in V·s/rad (equal to N·m/A); ω is speed in rad/s; V is the supply voltage; I is armature current in A; R<sub>a</sub> is armature resistance in Ω; T is torque in N·m.

Put together, ω = (V − I Ra) ÷ kΦ: a permanent-magnet motor runs fastest with no load, and its speed falls in a straight line as torque (and current) rise, down to zero at the stall current V ÷ Ra. Output power is T ω. The connection of the field gives four types:

items: Permanent magnet: wipers, window lifts, seats, blowers, fuel pumps; small, cheap and efficient. Speed is set by the supply voltage (PWM or series resistors).
Series wound: field in series with the armature, so the field grows with current and the starting torque is very high: the classic starter motor.
Shunt wound (field in parallel, near-constant speed) and compound (both windings, some heavy-vehicle starters).
Electronically commutated (brushless DC): the magnets turn and an electronic three-phase bridge, timed from Hall sensors, replaces the brushes; long life for fuel pumps, coolant pumps and fans.

blocks.text: A three-phase machine has three stator windings 120° apart. Fed with three-phase current they make a magnetic field that rotates at the synchronous speed.
n<sub>s</sub> is synchronous speed in rpm; f is the supply frequency in Hz; p is the number of poles; s is the slip of an induction machine; n is the rotor speed in rpm.

items: Synchronous machine: the rotor carries magnets or a DC field and turns exactly at ns. The vehicle alternator is a claw-pole synchronous generator whose three-phase output a diode bridge rectifies; most hybrid and electric cars use a permanent-magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) for traction.
Induction (asynchronous) machine: the rotor has bars shorted by end rings; currents are induced only when it slips behind the field, so it runs a few percent below ns. Rugged and magnet-free.
Traction machines are fed from the battery through an inverter that makes three-phase current of variable frequency, so f, and with it ns, sets the speed.

blocks.text: Single-phase AC machines (universal motors, capacitor-start and shaded-pole induction motors) run from mains AC. They appear in vehicles only behind an inverter or in workshop equipment. A single-phase field pulsates rather than rotates, so these motors need a starting aid.

A motor's limit is heat. Its windings warm while it runs and cool while it rests, so the same motor can deliver more power for a short run than for a continuous one. The duty type (IEC 60034-1 names ten, S1 to S10) says which pattern the rating assumes. For periodic duties the cyclic duration factor is the on-time as a share of the cycle (the cycle is 10 minutes unless stated).
t<sub>on</sub> is the time under load and t<sub>off</sub> the rest time in one cycle, in the same units.

head: Duty
Pattern
Vehicle example
rows: Constant load long enough to reach thermal equilibrium
Constant load for a stated time (e.g. 10 min), then rest until cold
Identical on–off cycles, starting heat negligible; rated with its CDF
Window lift, wiper on intermittent, door lock
As S3 but starting (S4) or starting and electric braking (S5) heat counts
Continuous running with periodic or non-periodic load and speed changes
Traction motor over a drive cycle (S9)

blocks.text: A starter motor is the extreme short-time case: rated for a cranking run of a few tens of seconds, after which it must cool. A short-time motor on continuous duty overheats.

examples.question: A 12 V permanent-magnet blower motor has armature resistance R<sub>a</sub> = 0.2 Ω and machine constant kΦ = 0.02 V·s/rad. Ignore friction. Find (a) the no-load speed, (b) the speed, torque, output power and efficiency at 10 A, and (c) the stall current and stall torque.
steps: Output power: T ω = 0.20 × 500 = 100 W. Input power: V I = 12 × 10 = 120 W. Efficiency: 100 ÷ 120 = 83.3 % (the 20 W lost is I²R<sub>a</sub> = 10² × 0.2).
Check: the speed falls in a straight line from 600 rad/s at 0 N·m to 0 at 1.20 N·m; at 0.20 N·m that line gives 600 × (1 − 0.20 ÷ 1.20) = 500 rad/s, as found.
examples.answer: No load 5730 rpm; at 10 A: 4775 rpm, 0.20 N·m, 100 W out, 83.3 % efficient; stall 60 A and 1.20 N·m.

examples.question: In a test, a window-lift motor runs for 4 s and rests for 12 s, over and over. (a) Find the cyclic duration factor and name the duty type. (b) A traction PMSM has 8 poles and its inverter supplies 400 Hz. Find its speed. (c) An induction traction motor has 4 poles, is fed at 200 Hz and runs with 3 % slip. Find its speed.
steps: (a) CDF = 4 ÷ (4 + 12) × 100 % = 25 %. Identical on–off cycles with negligible starting heat: S3 25 %.
(b) A synchronous motor turns at n<sub>s</sub> = 120 f ÷ p = 120 × 400 ÷ 8 = 6000 rpm.
Check: only the synchronous motor turns at the 6000 rpm field speed; the induction motor needs its 180 rpm of slip.
examples.answer: S3 with a CDF of 25 %; the PMSM turns at 6000 rpm and the induction motor at 5820 rpm.

traps: A DC motor's current is not V ÷ R<sub>a</sub> while it runs: the back emf subtracts, I = (V − E) ÷ R<sub>a</sub>. V ÷ R<sub>a</sub> is the stall (starting) current.
Use ω in rad/s in E = kΦω and P = Tω; rpm × 2π ÷ 60 converts. Mixing rpm into P = Tω gives an answer about ten times too large.
n<sub>s</sub> = 120 f ÷ p uses the number of poles, not pole pairs; with pole pairs it is 60 f ÷ (pairs).
A rating means nothing without its duty type: a 300 W S2 10 min motor is not a 300 W continuous motor.
The alternator is a three-phase synchronous machine; its DC output comes from the diode rectifier, not from a commutator.

quiz.q: Name the four kinds of DC motor by field connection and give one vehicle use of each.
quiz.a: Permanent magnet (wiper, window lift), series wound (starter), shunt wound (constant-speed drives), compound (heavy-vehicle starter); electronically commutated brushless DC for pumps and fans.

quiz.q: State duty types S1, S2 and S3.
quiz.a: S1 continuous: constant load to thermal equilibrium. S2 short-time: constant load for a stated time, then rest until cold. S3 intermittent periodic: identical on–off cycles, rated with a cyclic duration factor, starting heat negligible.

quiz.q: Why does a series-wound motor suit an engine starter?
quiz.a: The field current is the armature current, so at standstill the large current makes a strong field and torque rises roughly with the square of current; it gives the very high breakaway torque needed to crank a cold engine.

quiz.q: Explain why an induction motor must run below synchronous speed.
quiz.a: Rotor current is induced only when the rotor bars cut the rotating field. At synchronous speed there is no relative motion, no induced current and no torque, so the rotor settles at the slip that gives the torque the load needs.

quiz.q: A 12 V PM motor has R<sub>a</sub> = 0.5 Ω and draws 4 A at 3000 rpm. Find the back emf and kΦ.
A radiator fan motor rated S2 30 min is fitted to a car that idles in Chennai traffic for two hours. Predict what happens and recommend a fix.
quiz.a: The fan runs continuously, which is S1 duty. The S2 motor reaches its temperature limit after about 30 minutes and keeps heating: insulation and brushes age, the thermal cut-out trips and the engine overheats. Fit an S1-rated motor of the same output, or a larger S2 motor whose continuous rating covers the load.

beyond: Not for the exam. Traction machines use hairpin windings and oil cooling for high power density, and 48 V belt starter-generators merge the starter and alternator. Search for PMSM field-oriented control, hairpin stator winding, belt starter generator and IEC 60034-1 duty types.
